chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Bassam al-Sayrāfī from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the dung-eating camel, he said: 'Its meat is not to be eaten, nor is it to be ridden for forty days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating and riding a dung-eating camel (jalalah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the ruling of 'jalalah' for camels, specifying that their meat is impermissible and they should not be ridden for forty days to allow impurities to clear from their bodies. In Shia jurisprudence, this period is critical for purifying the animal's flesh, reflecting the broader principle of removing physical and spiritual impurity (najasah) from consumables. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Imams' direct teachings on dietary laws.
